summary.text: A 12-year-old girl, followed for six years for celiac disease, was brought to pediatric gastroenterology with painless abdominal distension. Examination found a palpable abdominal mass crossing the midline, with normal weight and height for age and otherwise normal systemic examination.

She reported full compliance with her gluten-free diet and had no anemia; anti-gliadin and anti-endomysium IgA were negative. Abdominal radiography showed no pathological finding and ultrasonography detected no pathological condition, but computed tomography showed soft tissue densities possibly compatible with a bezoar in the stomach.

After surgical approval, a trichobezoar shaped like the stomach and stretching towards the small intestine was removed, and the case was reported as Rapunzel syndrome. She had been pulling out and eating her hair over the last year.

Child psychiatry evaluation found explicit anxiety and depressive complaints; sertraline 50 mg/day and cognitive and behavioral techniques therapy were given, and her trichophagia regressed completely. She has been followed for the last year since the operation.
